name: Artemis III
short_status: Announced: crewed low Earth orbit demonstration, targeted 2027 (as of 2 November 2026)

facts.label: Orbit
facts.value: Low Earth orbit: the Blue Moon pathfinder waits in a circular orbit about 273 miles up, Orion circularizes at about 345 miles before closing in, and the Starship pathfinder flies lower, at 206 nautical miles, or about 237 miles (per NASA, 23 October 2026)

facts.label: Vehicle
facts.value: SLS with Orion, the first Orion to fly with a docking system installed; a spacer without propulsion takes the place of the rocket’s upper stage

facts.label: Docking targets
facts.value: About two days docked to Blue Origin’s Blue Moon pathfinder, then a docking test of up to two hours with SpaceX’s Starship pathfinder (per NASA, 23 October 2026)

facts.label: Backup crew
facts.value: Bob Hines (NASA), pilot of SpaceX Crew-4

facts.label: Recovery
facts.value: Pacific Ocean splashdown off California, recovered by NASA and the U.S. Navy
